limitations: Each timed sample is one measure() call: kernel computation plus the in-WASM serde_json::to_string() encoding of the full 119-column result, matching what a real worker caller actually receives. It is a worker round-trip-per-call time, not an isolated kernel time.
wasm_linear_memory_bytes_after_run is WebAssembly.Memory.buffer.byteLength read once after all 12 fixtures ran, not a tracked peak.
Single run, single machine, localhost static file server (no network latency, no HTTP compression on the preview server beyond what Node default serving provides). Not a production CDN measurement.

Browser timer resolution here was coarse (0.1-0.2ms granularity); the smallest workload (touching_gradient) is near that resolution floor, so its reported median has more relative noise than the larger workloads.
